Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old man with new-onset intermittent frontal headaches, decreased appetite/5 lb unintentional weight loss, bilateral hand tingling, episodic palpitations and breathlessness, and decreased libido that began around a job change; has history of hyperthyroidism on thyroxine. Plan: in-person clinic examination (cardiorespiratory and cardiac exam) and blood tests for thyroid status; no new medications today.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Intermittent severe frontal headaches affecting work.
  - Reduced appetite and ~5 lb unintentional weight loss.
  - Intermittent bilateral hand tingling (described as “quick picking”).
  - Episodic palpitations (heart “beating kind of fast”), about once daily or more.
  - Shortness of breath at rest/while sitting at desk.
  - Decreased libido.
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms began roughly when he changed jobs; all have been present since that time.
  - Headaches occur primarily during work (in meetings or while at laptop); occur randomly and usually one symptom at a time rather than all simultaneously.
  - Weight loss is recent and unintentional (about 5 lb).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Symptoms commonly occur during work; patient reports high work-related stress (rated 7–8/10).
  - No clear relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms/ROS mentioned:
  - Headaches associated with mild nausea; described shortness of breath and palpitations.
  - No lower extremity paresthesia; tingling limited to both hands.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No prior history of recurrent headaches before current symptoms.
  - No recreational drug use reported.
  - No current smoking.
  - No other medical problems reported beyond hyperthyroidism.

Past Medical History:
- Hyperthyroidism — on treatment (thyroxine). No complications documented.

Medications:
- Thyroxine — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Patient reports he is taking his thyroid medication as prescribed.

Allergies:
- None reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Lawyer in London; work involves ~50% computer/reading and 50% meetings.
- Work stress: rates current stress 7–8/10.
- Alcohol: drinks about once weekly, “a couple of glasses of wine.”
- Tobacco: denies smoking.
- Recreational drugs: denies use; specifically denies cocaine and marijuana.
- No other social or financial factors documented.

Family History:
- No family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented in the transcript.
- Vitals: not documented.

Investigations:
- No test results available.
- Plan noted for blood tests for thyroxine/thyroid function (tests to be performed in clinic).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Intermittent severe frontal headaches with associated nausea
  - Assessment: New-onset headaches temporally associated with job change; occurring primarily during work activities.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange in-person clinic visit for examination.
    - Perform focused head/neurologic assessment during clinic visit.
    - Further investigations to be determined after clinical exam.
- Issue 2: Palpitations and shortness of breath
  - Assessment: Episodic palpitations (~daily) and breathlessness at rest; patient has history of hyperthyroidism.
  - Plan:
    - In-person cardiac and respiratory examination in clinic.
    - Consider thyroid function testing (blood tests for thyroxine) to assess adequacy of thyroid treatment.
    - No new medications to be started today; clinician deferred prescribing until after in-person assessment.
- Issue 3: Bilateral hand tingling, decreased appetite, weight loss (~5 lb), decreased libido
  - Assessment: New symptoms beginning with job change; possible systemic contribution (patient has hyperthyroidism) — definitive cause not established in transcript.
  - Plan:
    - Review of systems and focused neurologic exam in clinic.
    - Thyroid blood tests as above.
    - Advise patient to book clinic appointment via app; clinician will communicate summary to clinic so history need not be fully repeated.
- General plan items:
  - Patient advised to attend in-person clinic appointment for examination and blood tests.
  - Continue current thyroxine as prescribed (patient reports adherence).
  - No immediate pharmacologic treatment started remotely.
  - Follow-up based on clinic findings and laboratory results.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation) are not documented.
  - Physical examination findings are not documented (no cardiac, respiratory, neurologic, or ENT exam documented).
  - Thyroxine dose/route/frequency is not documented.
  - No laboratory or ECG results available.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Doctor initially recorded “feeling hot” for the patient; patient did not confirm feeling hot but described episodes of shortness of breath that may correspond to that entry — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/text quality adequate with minimal inaudible portions; clinician and patient responses largely clear.
